newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bans corruption suspects from travelling.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bans corruption suspects from travelling.

text.p: Bulgaria's National Investigation Service (NIS) will seize the passports of more than 1,500 Bulgarians suspected of involvement in corruption, state radio said on Monday.

"Under an order of the National Investigation Service 1,581 Bulgarians, including bankers, former ministers and former deputies and credit millionaires, must go to the police and surrender their passports," the radio said.
Police began sending letters on July 11 to 200 insurance companies suspected of racketeering, seeking the return of travel documents of their senior staff, according to the radio.
NIS officials were not immediately available for further comment.
Crime has soared in Bulgaria since the collapse of one-party communist rule in 1989.
The government, which took office in May, has vowed to crack down on an organised crime spree that Prime Minister Ivan Kostov has said threatens the functioning of the state.
Parliament on Friday adopted amendments to the penal code toughening outdated legislation. It is expected to adopt updates to the criminal code this week before starting the summer recess.
